_meta.indication: Treatment of both the first-stage (hemolymphatic) and second-stage (meningoencephalitic) human African trypanosomiasis (HAT) due to Trypanosoma brucei gambiense in patients 6 years of age and older and weighing at least 20 kg

pivotal_trials.phase: Adequate and well-controlled randomized noninferiority (NI) trial (pivotal trial)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, active-controlled noninferiority trial comparing fexinidazole to NECT (nifurtimox-eflornithine combination therapy)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥ 15 years of age with late second-stage (stage 2) g-HAT due to Trypanosoma brucei gambiense, with evidence of parasites in blood, lymph and/or CSF at enrollment
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Clinical success (cure or probable cure) at 18 months after end of treatment in the mITT population
pivotal_trials.n: N=394, randomized 2:1 to fexinidazole (n=264) or NECT (n=130)
pivotal_trials.result: Clinical success at 18 months (mITT): 239/262 (91.2%) fexinidazole vs 124/127 (97.6%) NECT; difference -6.4% (95% CI -11.6%, -0.1%), meeting the prespecified NI margin of -13% but significantly less effective than NECT

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >10%): headache, vomiting, insomnia, nausea, asthenia, tremor, decreased appetite, dizziness, hypocalcemia, dyspepsia, back pain, upper abdominal pain, hyperkalemia. Warnings include QT prolongation, neuropsychiatric adverse reactions, neutropenia (15/264 [5.7%] vs 4/130 [3.1%] NECT), and potential hepatotoxicity. A numerical mortality imbalance was noted (fexinidazole 9/264 [3.4%] vs NECT 2/130 [1.5%] at month 24).
target_moa: Trypanocidal nitroimidazole antimicrobial; bioactivated by reduction via NADH-dependent, type I nitroreductase (NTR) enzymes in trypanosomatids to generate toxic reactive amines

advisory_committee.vote: Not discussed at an Advisory Committee meeting as no specific input from the committee or external consultants was needed

summary.text: Fexinidazole is a new chemical entity that received orphan drug designation (April 4, 2016) for HAT and a priority review; the sponsor also requested a tropical disease priority review voucher. The initial NDA (received March 12, 2020) received a Complete Response on November 12, 2020 over labeling disagreement; it was approved on the Class 1 Resubmission received May 18, 2021.
